title: Risk-weighted intake & customer communications playbook for private/VPC/on-prem requests
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable intake and comms playbook that product, solutions, and support use to triage private/VPC/on-prem customer requests involving networking constraints, version upgrades, and air-gapped environments. Goal: reduce time-to-decision, surface engineering/ops cost clearly to customers, and centralize risk scoring to enable objective prioritization for Dedicated and Private projects.
acceptance_criteria: A 5-step intake form (support/SE template) exists and is documented in Confluence with field-level guidance
A 3-level risk score (Low/Medium/High) is defined with mapping to recommended routing (self-serve, SE-assisted, sales-engage)
Email/Slack comms templates for each routing decision are available and reviewed by Legal/Support
A lightweight network compatibility checklist and minimal packet-level requirements are published and linked in the playbook
Hand-off criteria to Eng (ENG- queue) and timelines (SLA for initial engineering assessment) are in the playbook
intake_form_fields: Customer company size and deployment priority (pilot/production)
Desired deployment mode: Private/VPC/On-prem and expected region/colo
Network topology summary (eg. NAT, private peering, firewall policies, egress restrictions)
Are systems air-gapped? (yes/no/partial) — describe data in/out approach
Upgrade constraints: allowed maintenance windows, automated update policy (auto/manual), pinned runtime versions
Compliance requirements: SOC2/HIPAA/ISO, required audit logs/KMS/HSM
Expected QPS/peak tokens per second and concurrency profile
Third-party dependencies that need outbound access (package repos, telemetry, metrics exporters)
risk_scoring_rubric: Low: Non-airgapped, supports outbound egress to Redwood endpoints, upgrade windows flexible — route to self-serve or SE-assisted
Medium: Partial airgap or strict egress but accepts limited approved egress to vendor CDNs, pinned runtime needed — route to SE-assisted with solutions architecture review
High: Fully air-gapped, must be on-prem with no outbound, custom KMS/HSM, non-standard OS/kernel, or regulatory blockers — route to Sales + Engineering with formal SOW and enterprise onboarding
network_compatibility_checklist: Required TCP/UDP ports (detailed list linked): control plane, telemetry, metrics, healthchecks
DNS resolution requirements and fallback strategies for short-lived instances
Allowed cipher suites and TLS versions for mTLS (if mutual TLS is required)
Bandwidth baselines per expected tokens/sec and recommended burst capacity
Outbound dependency list: container registry, CRL/OCSP, time sync (NTP), license verification endpoints
Proxy and HTTP(S) interception guidance and certificate pinning implications
communication_templates: Template A - Low risk (self-serve): thanks for the details, next steps include our published install guide and access to the private-deploy quickstart; we optionally offer SE time for $X/hr

Template B - Medium risk (SE-assisted): recommended next step is a 60-minute technical discovery with Solutions Engineering. We'll run the network compatibility checklist and provide a mitigation plan within 7 business days.

Template C - High risk (Enterprise onboarding): require NDA/SOW. Assign Sales/Account Exec and schedule a cross-functional kickoff with Eng, Security, and Infra. Provide timeline estimate and build cost prelim within 10 business days.
decision_tradeoffs: Favoring faster time-to-response (SE-assisted) increases upfront deflection but may surface complex engineering work later — mitigated by mandatory engineering intake for Medium/High scores
Strict enforcement of airflow for air-gapped sites reduces risk but increases sales friction and lengthens procurement cycles
Offering a minimal on-prem agent for partially air-gapped customers reduces custom one-off builds but requires sustained maintenance effort from Eng
open_questions: Should we publish a public compatibility matrix by OS/kernel and container runtime? Tradeoff: helpful for customers but may be stale without engineering investment
What pricing and packaging guardrails should Sales use for Medium vs High engagements? Need legal and finance input
Do we accept limited 'whitelisted egress' as a Standard Offering or only via custom SOW?
